349419.title: Uniform-mass conjecture for cycles
349419.statement:
Let $C_m$ be the cycle on $m$ edges, let $E(C_m)$ be its edge set, and let $\beta(C_m,1)$ be the optimization parameter defined in the paper. **Uniform-mass conjecture for cycles.** For all $m\geq 3$, $\beta(C_m,1)$ is achieved by the uniform distribution on $E(C_m)$. In particular,

$$
\beta(C_m,1)=m^{-m}.

The paper explains that this is open in general; it considers the cases $m=5,6$ approachable, while its methods do not settle $m=7$.

355934.title: Saxton's permanent submatrix conjecture
355934.statement:
Let $B\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ be a matrix. For each $j\in[m]$, let the support of its $j$th column be $\{i\in[n]:B_{ij}\neq 0\}$. **Saxton's conjecture.** If, for every $J\subset[m]$,

$$
\left|\bigcup_{j\in J}\{i\in[n]:B_{ij}\neq 0\}\right|\geq 2|J|-1,
$$

then $B$ contains an $m\times m$ submatrix with non-zero permanent. If true, this would imply that every essential cover of the $n$-cube has at least $\lceil n/2\rceil+1$ hyperplanes, matching the best-known constructions; the supplied source does not establish whether the conjecture is resolved.

356476.title: Quadruple equidistribution conjecture for ascent-sequence statistics
356476.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}_n$ be the set of ascent sequences of length $n$, and let $\mathsf{asc}$, $\mathsf{rep}$, $\mathsf{zero}$ and $\mathsf{max}$ denote their ascent-sequence statistics.

$$
\sum_{s\in\mathcal{A}_n}u^{\mathsf{asc}(s)}x^{\mathsf{rep}(s)}z^{\mathsf{zero}(s)}q^{\mathsf{max}(s)}=\sum_{s\in\mathcal{A}_n}u^{\mathsf{rep}(s)}x^{\mathsf{asc}(s)}z^{\mathsf{max}(s)}q^{\mathsf{zero}(s)}.
$$

Equivalently, the statistic quadruples $(\mathsf{asc},\mathsf{rep},\mathsf{zero},\mathsf{max})$ and $(\mathsf{rep},\mathsf{asc},\mathsf{max},\mathsf{zero})$ are equidistributed on ascent sequences. The source states that this conjecture is affirmed in the paper, so it is no longer open.

\{x,y,x+y,xy\}

356748.title: Classification conjecture for perfect restricted s-bases
356748.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, and let $m\geq2$ and $s\geq2$ be integers. A **perfect restricted $s$-basis** of size $m$ is a subset whose restricted sums of at most $s$ elements represent every element of $G$ uniquely. **Perfect restricted basis classification conjecture.** Such a basis exists if and only if $G$ has order $2^m$, or $G$ is isomorphic to one of

$$
\mathbb Z_{2^{s+1}-1},\quad \mathbb Z_2^{2s},\quad \mathbb Z^{2s-2}\times\mathbb Z_4.
$$

The paper gives examples in each listed family and a complete classification only for restricted $2$-bases; the asserted classification for all $m,s\geq2$ remains open.

356961.title: Hajebi's conjecture on subquadratic clique covers of K_{t,t}-free graphs
356961.statement:
Let $t\ge 1$ be an integer. A graph is **$K_{t,t}$-free** if it has no induced copy of the complete bipartite graph $K_{t,t}$, and a clique cover is a collection of cliques covering every edge.

$$
O\left(|G|^{2-\varepsilon}\right).
$$

The conjecture is attributed to Sepehr Hajebi, who proposed it at a conference in Lyon. The paper proves a related bound with $\varepsilon=1/(2t)$, so the proposed statement is solved by the result described in the source.

357849.title: Super vertex total local antimagic labeling existence conjecture
357849.statement:

$$
w(v)=\sum_{x\in NT(v)}f(x),\qquad NT(v)=N(v)\cup\{uv:uv\in E\},
$$

and additionally $f(V)=\{1,2,\dots,|V|\}$. **The super vertex total local antimagic labeling conjecture.** Every graph without isolated vertices admits a super vertex total local antimagic labeling. The paper presents this as an existence problem for a broad class of graph labelings; no resolution is supplied here.

381984.title: Axiom for the small quasi-kernel conjecture
381984.statement: Let $D$ be a non-empty digraph. For a vertex $u\in V(D)$, let $d^+(u)$ denote its out-degree, let $N^+[u]$ denote its closed out-neighborhood, and call a vertex a source if it has in-degree zero. **Axiom for the small quasi-kernel conjecture.** There exists a vertex $u\in V(D)$ such that $d^+(u)>0$ and $D-N^+[u]$ has at most $d^+(u)$ sources not present in $D$. If this axiom holds for every directed graph, the paper's preceding argument proves the small quasi-kernel conjecture, namely that every source-free directed graph has a quasi-kernel of size at most half its vertices.

382041.title: Ivančo's supermagic labeling conjecture for Cartesian products of cycles
382041.statement: Let $C_n$ and $C_m$ be cycles with $n,m\geq 3$. A **supermagic labeling** of a graph with $q$ edges is a bijection from its edge set to $\{1,2,\dots,q\}$ such that the sums of the labels on edges incident with each vertex are equal. **Ivančo's conjecture.** The Cartesian product $C_n\Box C_m$ has a supermagic labeling for every $n,m\geq 3$. The conjecture extends the known cases of equal cycle lengths and of products of two even cycles; its general status is not specified in the source.
